items.title: The GM panel's Next line answered 'everyone has acted' with Edit campaign: six presses, the day and session bumped by hand, and with the refill box off none of the boundary work ran; no one-press advance on the panel
items.old_state: fixed in 1.2.43 (AUDIT-1.2.42.md 2.2; commit 90c17021, 12.09.2026; the first tag that contains it is v1.2.44, this clone has no v1.2.43 tag): the Next line runs action 'eclipse', and a 'Next time of day' button stands beside the clock
items.evidence: gm-panel.mjs:996-999: with nobody left to act the line's action is "eclipse" (boundary.mjs:96 toggleEclipse, the function the HUD's chevron calls). gm-panel.mjs:418-421 and 1122-1128: the clock line carries an Advance button (en.json:5179 'Skip the Eclipse') that runs boundary.mjs:134-144 nextTimeOfDay -> advanceTimeOfDay({ resetActions: true }), refused during an Eclipse (boundary.mjs:136-139). That call does the whole boundary (clock.mjs:784-857: overflow check, refill, restock, seals, motive tick, SYNC.clock). Edit campaign's Apply is a correction whose box only refills (gm-campaign.mjs:370-384).
items.pinned_by: R28 (tier 0, '"Move the clock on" runs the Eclipse', tests-tier0.mjs:2447); R1194 (tier 0, one road for the Eclipse); R3406 (tier 1, the Advance button in every state); tier 2 E37-T2
items.refutation_tried: Looked for another UI road that still sends the GM to the editor to move the hour: nextStep has no 'jump' action left (grep of gm-panel.mjs: 0 hits), Edit campaign is no tile of the panel (gm-panel.mjs:274-280), and the editor's own time-of-day select stays a correction that calls a pending assembly off first (gm-campaign.mjs:53-59, 357-359).
items.note: Since E37 C3 both roads open a readiness round first when a connected player owns a student (boundary.mjs:105-107, 140-142; the owner's ask of 28.10.2026 quoted in boundary.mjs:12-15), so the count is two presses plus the round. A start also asks one question first (boundary.mjs:104; Q-E37-3).

new_observations.title: A bystander's stopwatch counts through a pause that begins during an incident
new_observations.what: While an incident hides the clock, paintElapsed reads this page's copy from before the incident, whose pausedAt and pausedTotalMs are the old ones. A pause that starts meanwhile freezes the participants' and the GMs' minutes line but not the bystander's (elapsedOf takes 'now' when the copy has no pausedAt), and after the unpause the break is not taken off until the incident ends, when the reading drops by its length. No secret is shown; two screens disagree for the incident's length.

new_observations.title: The JSDoc of advanceTimeOfDay names a caller that no longer calls it and denies the one that does
new_observations.what: It says resetActions is off 'and nothing in the ordinary flow turns it on any more', and that the GM panel's 'also refill' checkbox is 'the one remaining caller'. Today the panel's 'Skip the Eclipse' button passes resetActions: true (boundary.mjs:143), and the checkbox does not call advanceTimeOfDay at all (gm-campaign.mjs:379-384 calls resetAllActions and SearchTokens.reset).

new_observations.title: migrate.mjs's header still states that '-=key' can be accepted and do nothing, against the reading on 14.370
new_observations.what: The header and the first clause's note say a '-=key' delete 'can be accepted and do nothing at all' and 'cannot be trusted to remove anything in this Foundry'. The reading of 16.11.2026 on Foundry 14.370 (docs/dev/e39/CALIBRATION.md:20, LIVE-E30-01, repeated in the repository's own working notes) is that it does delete and writes a deprecation warning. The rule the comment draws (read back after a removal) is unaffected.

new_observations.title: DRPG.Clock.eclipseStillOn says one thing more in Polish than in English
new_observations.what: English: 'End it from the clock's chevron; until then no incident can open.' Polish adds 'a przejscia licza sie do limitu Eclipse' (and crossings count against the Eclipse's limit). The key parity check compares keys, not sentences, so a GM reading English is not told the second consequence.
